baseline.observation: Both shell workers repeated release-apply after every failure, including the previous real EAGAIN response read; a later success did not resolve the first accepted request. A readiness failure after receipt acceptance could also restart POST.

implementation.transport: exchange_checked has BeforeSubmission only before the first possible HTTP write; every later error remains Unconfirmed. Existing exchange wrapper preserves standalone once-only callers.
implementation.application_rejection: Only complete HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict with one exact numeric error -23 allows a new startup attempt. Strict fields reject duplicates, extensions, quoted numbers and trailing data. All other errors are terminal.
implementation.proof_boundary: DNS release_command returns incompatible target before submit_command. Catalog release application validates assignments and the complete plan before release/deployment/operational publication; a negative application result may itself be committed. Snapshot-equality regression covers initially absent and installed releases, then a valid new-boot target report permits admission of the same command.
implementation.deadline: Read exact signed envelope once, retain one checked monotonic deadline through startup and accepted observation; per-request cap never extends it; startup backoff min(1s, original remaining).
implementation.fixture: Existing bounded serial loop observes listener and initial single-node DNS leader markers before invoking one release-apply command with original fixture budget left. Ready only on success. Worker failure ends the loop; neither marker proves completion or rollback.
implementation.ownership: Existing C18 host envelope and TcpStream scopes; no new kernel root, pin, registry, custody or recovery family. Socket disposal cannot cancel accepted remote work.
